diagnostic_evidence.quote: All three methods exhibit a time complexity of $O(N^2)$ and outperform S-Fair-SC.
However, Figure \ref{fg - GermanRunTime} reveals that AFF-Fair-SMW incurred the highest overall runtime, while the remaining algorithms exhibited similar performance.
As shown in Figure \ref{fg - LastfmBalance}, our algorithms maintained an average balance comparable to S-Fair-SC.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract asserts the method is 'flexible enough to achieve twice as much balance' and 'twice as fast as the state-of-the-art', and the introduction asserts all three variants 'outperform S-Fair-SC'. The paper establishes no balance guarantee beyond comparability (experiments report average balance 'comparable to S-Fair-SC', with fluctuations sometimes underperforming it), and its own Experiment 4 reports that AFF-Fair-SMW has the highest overall runtime on German, contradicting a blanket outperformance claim. The prose thus claims quantitatively doubled balance and universal runtime superiority that nothing in the paper establishes.

failure_location.quote: We achieve an improvement in computation time that is twice as fast as the state-of-the-art, and also flexible enough to achieve twice as much balance.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the abstract/introductory sentences to what is supported: balance comparable to baselines, runtime improvements in specific regimes (sparse graphs, eigs-dominated cases), with the German exception acknowledged.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised performance guarantees (2x balance, universal superiority over S-Fair-SC) are not supported by any formal result or experiment in the paper.
issues.title: Abstract and introduction overclaim balance and runtime results
issues.why_classification: A local rewording of unsupported prose preserves every theorem, guarantee and experimental finding; no mathematical content is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: &= G^{-1} H - F\Lambda - \mu F F^T H

issues.failure_explanation: For the minimization problem (SMW2) the augmented-Lagrangian penalty for the constraint F^T H = 0 must enter with a plus sign, mu/2*||F^T H||_F^2. The displayed Lagrangian has -mu/2*||F^T H||_F^2, i.e. the 'penalty' rewards violating the fairness constraint. Consequences inside the source: the stationarity system uses (G^{-1} - mu FF^T), and the Lambda=0 subproblem min_H (1/2)Tr(H^T(G^{-1}-mu FF^T)H) is unbounded below along directions with F^T x != 0, so it is not a well-posed subproblem. The next display (SMW3) then silently restores the sign (+mu F F^T) and re-imposes H^T H = I without any derivation. As written, the Augmented-Lagrangian derivation never yields problem (SMW3), although (SMW3) is the sensible penalty formulation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the sign of the penalty term in the Lagrangian display and in the block system (G^{-1} - mu FF^T -> G^{-1} + mu FF^T), and state the H-subproblem under the orthonormality constraint H^T H = I; then (SMW3) follows routinely.
issues.overall_effect: The central derivation connecting (SMW2) to (SMW3)/(reformulation) is unsound as written; the algorithmic object itself is unaffected once the sign is fixed, since (SMW3) is the standard penalty formulation.
issues.title: Augmented Lagrangian derivation uses a wrong-sign penalty, so problem (SMW3) is never derived
issues.why_classification: A local sign repair of the Lagrangian display restores the intended derivation; (SMW3), (reformulation) and the algorithm are unchanged, so no substantive claim or guarantee is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Therefore the eigenvalues of $B=\frac{1}{2}(D^{-1}W+WD^{-1})$ belong in $[-1,1]$
and the matrix $G_{rw}$ is generalized positive definite because its symmetric part $C$ is positive definite.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof infers that B = (1/2)(D^{-1}W + WD^{-1}) has eigenvalues in [-1,1] from the (true) fact that the eigenvalues of the non-normal matrix D^{-1}W lie in [-1,1]. That inference is invalid (the Rayleigh quotient of a non-normal matrix is not controlled by its eigenvalues) and the claimed bound is false: for the star graph K_{1,4} the symmetric part B has eigenvalues +/-5/4, so |x^T B x / x^T x| reaches 5/4 > 1. Hence lambda_min(C) = 2 + lambda_min(B) is not bounded below by 1. Worse, the theorem statement itself is false: for a star with n >= 15 vertices, lambda_min(B) = -n/(2*sqrt(n-1)) < -2, so x^T G_rw x = x^T (B + 2I) x < 0 for some x, contradicting 'generalized positive definite'. (The proof also refers to an undefined matrix 'S'.)

failure_location.quote: $G_{rw}$ has real eigenvalues and is generalized positive definite. That is $\bm{x}^T G_{rw}\bm{x} >0$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the theorem as: D^{-1}W is similar to D^{-1/2}WD^{-1/2}, hence G_rw has real eigenvalues in [1,3] and is invertible; drop the false quadratic-form (generalized positive definiteness) claim, which cannot be true.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed justification that G_rw is a valid (positive definite) choice of G fails; the real-eigenvalue/invertibility part needed by the RW variant survives only through the similarity argument, not through this theorem as stated.
issues.title: Theorem that G_rw is generalized positive definite is false and its proof uses a false spectral claim
issues.why_classification: The stated positive-definiteness claim must be abandoned (it is false), but the property the RW variant actually needs - real spectrum in [1,3] and invertibility - is established inside the same proof by the similarity argument, so a contained restatement preserves the method without new architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $D^{-1}$ is an invertible diagonal matrix, it is of full rank, and multiplying by it from the right does not change the row space $ \mathcal{R}(F^T D^{-1}) = \mathcal{R}(F^T) $

issues.failure_explanation: The proof hinges on the identity F^T D^{-1} = F^T D^{-1} F (F^T F)^{-1} F^T, i.e. F^T D^{-1} = F^T D^{-1} P_F, which holds iff the rows of F^T D^{-1} lie in the row space of F^T. The claimed justification ('multiplying by an invertible diagonal matrix from the right does not change the row space') is false: right multiplication by an invertible diagonal matrix preserves only the rank, not the row space. Concrete counterexample: path 1-2-3 with w12 = 1, w23 = 2, groups V1 = {1,3}, V2 = {2}, so F = (1/2, -1, -1/2)^T and D = diag(1,3,2). Then F^T D^{-1} = (1/2, -1/3, -1/4), while F^T D^{-1} F (F^T F)^{-1} F^T = (17/24)(2/3) F^T = (17/72, -17/36, -17/72), which is different. With the identity false, the rewriting of P, the assertion that W P is symmetric, and hence the similarity U_rw ~ D^{-1/2} W P D^{-1/2} to a symmetric matrix all collapse; the theorem is left unproven.

failure_location.quote: The eigenvalues of $U_{\text{rw}} = G_{\text{rw}}(I-F(F^T G_{\text{rw}}F)^{-1}F^T G_{\text{rw}})$ are real.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must provide a valid proof that the spectrum of U_rw = G_rw(I - F(F^T G_rw F)^{-1} F^T G_rw) is real (or restrict the RW variant to regimes where a corrected statement holds), since the identity (eq:identity) used by the source is false in general and cannot be fixed locally.
issues.overall_effect: The only theoretical support for the RW-Fair-SMW variant (real spectrum of U_rw, needed for the eigensolver step) is lost; no labelled downstream result relies on it, but the advertised RW variant is left unjustified.
issues.title: Proof that U_rw has real eigenvalues uses a false identity
issues.why_classification: The single proof strategy offered fails at a demonstrably false identity, the statement may itself be false, and the source contains no alternative argument; either a genuinely new proof is required or the real-spectrum guarantee for the advertised RW variant must be abandoned.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \State Construct the fairness-adjusted matrix $U_{\text{sym}} = G_{\mathrm{sym}} - M (F^T M)^{-1} F^T G_{\mathrm{sym}}$

issues.failure_explanation: The derivation and Theorems 3 and 6 concern the matrix U = G - G F (F^T G F)^{-1} F^T G, obtained from the Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury limit of (G^{-1} + mu F F^T)^{-1}. Algorithm alg:smw-cluster instead computes M = G_sym^{-1} F and builds U = G - G^{-1}F (F^T G^{-1} F)^{-1} F^T G, which is a different matrix (G^{-1} appears where G should). It is in general not symmetric, so its top-k eigenvectors need not form the orthonormal basis the analysis requires and may be complex; none of the paper's results apply to it. Example: G = diag(1,4), F = (1,1)^T gives U_alg = [[0.2, -3.2], [-0.2, 3.2]] (non-symmetric) instead of the symmetric [[0.2, -0.8], [-0.8, 1]].

failure_location.quote: \State Compute the projection matrix $M = G_{\mathrm{sym}}^{-1} F$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace step 2 by M = G_sym F (equivalently M(F^T M)^{-1}F^T G_sym = G_sym F (F^T G_sym F)^{-1} F^T G_sym); with this one-word change the algorithm computes exactly the matrix analyzed in (reformulation) and Theorems 3/6, and every guarantee is restored.
issues.overall_effect: The executable procedure does not implement the fairness-adjusted operator derived in (reformulation) and analyzed by Theorems 3 and 6; its output carries no fairness or spectral guarantee.
issues.title: Fair-SMW algorithm computes a different matrix than the analyzed U
issues.why_classification: A single local, forced correction to one algorithm step makes the implemented matrix coincide with the analyzed symmetric U, preserving all substantive claims; no new argument is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof chain only establishes the upper bound y^T(D-W)y / y^T D y <= 2; its final line evaluates the value of that upper bound, not the supremum. The supremum equals the largest eigenvalue of the normalized Laplacian, which is strictly smaller than 2 unless the graph has a bipartite component containing an edge. Counterexample: the triangle (3-cycle, unit weights) has L_sym spectrum {0, 3/2, 3/2}, so the supremum is 3/2, not 2. The displayed identity is therefore false; only the inequality sup <= 2 is established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the displayed identity by sup <= 2 (noting equality holds iff some connected component is bipartite and contains an edge); all subsequent uses survive unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Only the theorem's own statement overclaims; the [0,2] eigenvalue bound that the paper actually invokes (for Theorems 2 and 4) remains valid from the same argument.
issues.title: Normalized-Laplacian bound asserted as an attained supremum
issues.why_classification: A one-symbol correction of the statement preserves the entire chain of results, since only the upper bound 2 is ever used; no rate, regime or guarantee is lost.
